meta.name: Frontier agents on public tau2-bench Telecom traces
meta.question: On public recorded tau2-bench Telecom runs, how often do five frontier models solve the task, how do they fail, and how far do newer models' answers at each recorded step drift from GPT-5.2's?
meta.domain: Telecom technical support (customer-service agent with a simulated user who runs the device actions)

conditions.name: recorded_full_runs
conditions.description: Exgentic's runs of tau2-bench Telecom with its tool_calling agent harness: one run per task per model, the model under test talking to a simulated user who performs the device actions. Outcomes are the dataset's success/score columns; nothing was re-run.

conditions.name: step_check_gpt52_recorded_calls
conditions.description: Kitaru's model-swap step check: 160 sampled recorded GPT-5.2 calls resent, as recorded (full conversation up to that step, the recorded tool list), to GPT-5.2 itself (noise floor) and 7 newer candidates; replies compared with GPT-5.2's recorded reply.

setup.prompt_rewriting_note: No prompt was changed. The agent's policy reaches the model as the first user message in the recordings, and the step check resends it unchanged.

tools.note: Every recorded tool definition has an empty parameter schema ({"type": "object", "properties": {}}); the step check passes them as recorded. Device tools (toggles, reboot, APN reset and others) belong to the simulated user, not the agent.

setup.user_simulator: tau2-bench's LLM user simulator, as run by Exgentic. Its calls were filtered out of this dataset, so its model and cost are not known here.

limits.recorded_full_runs_note: Step and token limits of the Exgentic harness are not recorded in the dataset.

judges.name: tau2-bench task evaluation, as recorded by Exgentic
judges.note: Read from the dataset's success column; not re-graded here.

grading.tie_break_note: No ranking ties were broken; the step check's analyzer 'Best for' rule (within 10 points of the reference's self-agreement) is reported as the analyzer gave it.
grading.human_agreement_note: No human review: outcomes come from the benchmark's evaluator, and the step check uses exact comparison.
grading.self_grading_check_note: No LLM judge was used, so no model graded its own output.

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: correct / n, where correct = runs with success=true. Every run counts in n.

metrics.name: cost_per_correct_cents
metrics.definition: 100 x (sum of the dataset's agent_cost over all n runs of the model, solved or not) / correct. agent_cost is Exgentic's figure for the agent-under-test model's calls; how it priced cached tokens is not documented in the dataset. benchmark_cost (the user simulator and evaluation) is excluded.

metrics.name: mean_tokens_per_case
metrics.definition: Mean of the dataset's total_tokens per run.

metrics.name: mean_calls_per_case
metrics.definition: Mean number of agent chat spans (model calls) per run.

metrics.name: tool_choice_rate
metrics.definition: Step check: among answered calls where the recorded GPT-5.2 reply called a tool, the share where the candidate called the same tool (arguments may differ). Kitaru analyzer field tool_choice_rate; Wilson 95% interval.

metrics.name: exact_agreement_rate
metrics.definition: Step check: among answered calls, the share with the same tool and same normalized arguments, or the same normalized text. Kitaru analyzer field agreement_rate; Wilson 95% interval.

metrics.name: step_cost_per_call_cents
metrics.definition: Step check: mean cost per answered call from the candidate's reported token usage at the price in models[] (cached input at the cached price where one is set).

noise.method: Recorded outcomes: one run per task per model, no repeats, so no outcome noise floor. Step check: GPT-5.2 resent its own 160 recorded calls once (the reference); its agreement with its own recording is the step-level noise floor.
noise.ci_method: Wilson score 95% interval for rates; paired candidate-minus-reference differences use a cluster bootstrap over recorded runs (swapbench.stats.paired_delta, 10000 resamples, seed 0).
noise.tie_threshold_note: No fixed tie threshold for outcomes; differences whose 95% interval includes 0 are reported as not distinguishable.

results_note: One row per recorded run; 0 duplicate cases. Scoring: success=true counts as correct; status 'unsuccessful' and status 'unknown' with success=false count as wrong; status 'unknown' with success=true counts as correct (the dataset's status and success columns disagree on those rows). No runs were dropped: these are third-party recordings, not our harness. Two GPT-5.2 rows carry a Claude or Gemini config_path; they are counted under the model their spans name.
per_type_note: Types come from text matching (see dataset.types_note); counts are small, so read per-type rates with caution.

failures.definition: An unsolved run (success=false) in which the agent called the transfer_to_human_agents tool. Detected from tool calls, not text. The policy allows a transfer only when the request cannot be handled within the agent's actions; these tasks were solvable.
failures.example: After walking the user through airplane mode, a SIM reseat, a network-mode change and an APN reset, the agent handed the case to a human while the user's data connection still failed, although the task was solvable.

failures.definition: An unsolved run (success=false) with no transfer_to_human_agents call. Detected from tool calls, not text.
failures.example: The agent declared that the on-device and account fixes it could perform were exhausted, or left the user with another question, and the conversation ended with the issue still open.

failures.definition: Any run in which an agent message says it does not have access to the device or device tools (regular-expression text matching on the agent's messages; a sub-pattern, also counted in one of the two categories above when the run was unsolved).
failures.example: Six steps in, the agent escalated, saying it could not run device diagnostics itself; in this benchmark the user runs the device tools on the agent's instructions.

failures_note: 117 of 143 unsolved runs ended in an escalation to a human. Categories come from tool calls, except claimed_no_device_access, which is text matching.

headline_findings.finding: On 499 public tau2-bench Telecom runs, Kimi K2.5 solved the most tasks and GPT-5.2 the fewest.
Most unsolved runs end with the agent handing the user to a human on a task it could have solved.
Re-sent its own recorded calls, GPT-5.2 picks the same tool only part of the time, which sets the bar any replacement has to be read against.
Of the seven newer candidates, only deepseek-v4.1-flash picked GPT-5.2's recorded tool clearly less often than GPT-5.2's own repeat; every other candidate's paired interval includes zero.
Unsolved runs cost more per task than solved ones for every model, so failures are also the expensive runs.

limitations: Recorded outcomes are one run per task per model, with no repeats, so no outcome noise floor was measured.
Runs cannot be paired by task across models (no task identifier in the public data), so model-vs-model differences are unpaired and only their separate Wilson intervals are reported.
The step check measures similarity to GPT-5.2's recorded replies, not correctness; no candidate's task success was measured, so it cannot say which model would solve more tasks.

Only one recorded model (GPT-5.2) could be reached for the step check; Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro, DeepSeek V3.2 and Kimi K2.5 as recorded were not reachable with the available keys, so step agreement could not be compared with recorded outcomes.
Recorded tool definitions have empty parameter schemas, so candidates saw tool names and descriptions but no argument schemas; this affects every candidate including the reference.

OpenAI rejected 19 of the 160 calls for every OpenAI candidate (a recorded tool-call id longer than OpenAI's 64-character limit); those calls are excluded from the OpenAI candidates' rates, so OpenAI and non-OpenAI candidates are scored on slightly different call sets.
9 of 1057 recorded GPT-5.2 calls were skipped by the analyzer for a missing tool schema.
The recorded GPT-5.2 settings (reasoning effort, temperature) are not in the data; the step check used provider defaults.
Issue types and the claimed_no_device_access category come from text matching, not human labels.
agent_cost is Exgentic's figure; its prices and cached-token treatment are undocumented, and the user simulator's cost is excluded.
Open-weight candidate prices in the step check are unverified third-party listings.
One step-check run's spend was not recorded (its result exceeded Kitaru's 1 MB worker task-result limit and was discarded), so total spend is null.
